name: manual_e4b689
claim: claude-sonnet-5-session is an approved value for the reviewer field in .agent/memory lesson/candidate records, alongside other model-designation session identifiers (e.g. claude-haiku-4-5-session, claude-opus-5-session, claude-fable-5-session/mythos-session) -- these are memory-schema attribution strings, NOT git commit author/committer identities, and must never be added to scripts/git/identity-policy.json (that file governs a completely different, email-keyed concern; noreply@anthropic.com already has allowed_names:[] there, meaning any commit-author name including these is already permitted for actual git commits)

decisions.notes: User explicitly requested these be added as approved attribution identities after CodeRabbit review #4998833290 flagged claude-sonnet-5-session appearing as a 'reviewer' field value in lessons.jsonl entries (lines 1094-1101) as a Major finding, apparently expecting it to match some enforced allowlist. Investigated: scan-tracked-banned-tokens.sh currently reports 0 issues (this string isn't actually banned), and no code anywhere validates the 'reviewer' field against any schema or allowlist -- .agent/tools/learn.py, graduate.py, and render_lessons.py never check it. Confirmed identity-policy.json (git commit email/name pairs, synced from orama canonical) is the wrong file: 'reviewer' isn't a git author/committer field, it's memory-schema metadata, and this file already fully permits any author name for noreply@anthropic.com. This lesson IS the fix -- documenting the decision that these identifiers are sanctioned memory-schema values is what CodeRabbit's finding was actually asking for, not a code change to an unrelated file.
